theory.intro: A **z-score** (or **standardised score**) tells you how many standard deviations a value sits from the mean. A positive $z$ means the value is above the mean; a negative $z$ means it is below.
facts: The formula is $z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$, where $x$ is the value, $\mu$ is the mean and $\sigma$ is the standard deviation. Use $\sigma>0$.
Subtract the mean from the value, never the other way round; reversing the subtraction reverses the sign of $z$.
A value above the mean gives a positive $z$, and a value below the mean gives a negative $z$.
A value equal to the mean gives $z = 0$.
The size of $z$ is a count of standard deviations, so $z = -1.5$ is $1.5$ standard deviations below the mean.
A $z$-score has no units, so it can be compared even when the raw values are marks, seconds or grams.
Round $z$ as the question directs; otherwise give two decimal places.
steps: Substitute the value, the mean and the standard deviation

workedExamples.question_text:
A machine produces packets with mean mass $42.6$ g and standard deviation $3.5$ g.
(a) Calculate the $z$-score for a packet of mass $48.8$ g.
(b) Calculate the $z$-score for a packet of mass $38.1$ g.
Give the $z$-scores correct to $2$ decimal places.
(c) Packets are rejected if their $z$-score is below $-1.5$ or above $1.5$. Which of these two packets is rejected?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Write $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$.
(a) $z=\dfrac{48.8-42.6}{3.5}=\dfrac{6.2}{3.5}$
$=1.771428\ldots\approx1.77$.
The packet is above the mean, so its score is positive.
(b) $z=\dfrac{38.1-42.6}{3.5}=\dfrac{-4.5}{3.5}$
$=-1.285714\ldots\approx-1.29$.
The packet is below the mean, so its score is negative.
(c) $1.771428\ldots>1.5$, so the $48.8$ g packet is rejected.
The other score is between $-1.5$ and $1.5$, so the $38.1$ g packet is accepted.

workedExamples.question_text:
A test has mean $57$ and standard deviation $8$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Student}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Mark}&69&51&57&61\end{array}$
(a) Calculate each student's standardised score.
(b) Describe B's result in terms of the mean and standard deviation.
(c) Which result, A or B, is further from the mean? By how many standard deviations further?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Use $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ for each mark.
A: $z=\dfrac{69-57}{8}=1.5$.
B: $z=\dfrac{51-57}{8}=-0.75$.
C: $z=\dfrac{57-57}{8}=0$.
D: $z=\dfrac{61-57}{8}=0.5$.
(b) B is $0.75$ standard deviations below the mean.
C's score of $0$ shows that the mark equals the mean, not that the mark is zero.
(c) A is $1.5$ standard deviations from the mean; B is $0.75$ standard deviations from it.
$1.5-0.75=0.75$.
A is further from the mean by $0.75$ standard deviations.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) The times (seconds) to solve a puzzle are $8,11,13,15,19$. Use a calculator to find the mean and population standard deviation, then calculate the $z$-score of the slowest time. Give the standard deviation and $z$-score correct to $2$ decimal places.
(b) Fun-run times have mean $18$ minutes $24$ seconds and standard deviation $1$ minute $40$ seconds. Calculate the $z$-score of a time of $16$ minutes $9$ seconds.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Enter all five times in statistics mode and read the population standard deviation.
$\mu=13.2$, $\sigma=3.709447\ldots\approx3.71$ seconds.
The slowest time is the largest, $x=19$.
Keep the unrounded standard deviation in the calculation.
$z=\dfrac{19-13.2}{3.709447\ldots}$
$=1.563575\ldots\approx1.56$.
(b) Use seconds throughout.
$\mu=18\times60+24=1104$, $\sigma=60+40=100$, $x=16\times60+9=969$.
$z=\dfrac{969-1104}{100}=\dfrac{-135}{100}=-1.35$.
All three time quantities must use the same unit.

foundation.question_text:
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 80$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 6$.
Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 68$.

A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 35$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 8$.
Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 47$.

A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 11.9$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 2.5$.
Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 13.4$.
What is the $z$-score of a value that lies $2.5$ standard deviations below the mean?
foundation.solution_text:
The $z$-score counts standard deviations from the mean, and below the mean is negative.
$z = -2.5$

foundation.question_text: The masses of apples in a crate have a mean of $145$ g and a standard deviation of $12$ g. Calculate the $z$-score of an apple with a mass of $154$ g.

Ella's $z$-score in a test was $-0.8$.
Describe her result in terms of the mean and standard deviation of the test.
foundation.solution_text:
The $z$-score is negative, so Ella's mark was below the mean.
Her mark was $0.8$ standard deviations below the mean of the test.

development.question_text:
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 34$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 6$.
Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 27$, correct to two decimal places.

The monthly rainfall at a weather station has a mean of $62$ mm and a standard deviation of $7.5$ mm.
Calculate the $z$-score of a month with $74$ mm of rain.

Travel times on a bus route have a mean of $38$ minutes and a standard deviation of $4.5$ minutes.
Calculate the $z$-score of a trip that takes $31$ minutes, correct to two decimal places.

In a test the mean was $64$ and the standard deviation was $8$.
Copy and complete the table of standardised scores.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{Student} & \text{Ana} & \text{Bo} & \text{Chi} & \text{Dev} \\ \hline \text{Mark} & 76 & 56 & 64 & 70 \\ \hline z\text{-score} & \ & \ & \ & \ \end{array}$

Annual rainfall in a town has a mean of $1180$ mm and a standard deviation of $145$ mm.
Calculate the $z$-score of a year with $995$ mm of rain, correct to two decimal places.

Two values from the same dataset have $z$-scores of $1.2$ and $-0.4$.
Which value is further from the mean, and by how many standard deviations further?
development.solution_text:
Distance from the mean is the size of the $z$-score, ignoring its sign.
The first value is $1.2$ standard deviations from the mean and the second is $0.4$ standard deviations from the mean.
$1.2 - 0.4 = 0.8$
The value with $z = 1.2$ is further from the mean, by $0.8$ standard deviations.

mastery.question_text:
The times, in seconds, taken by eight students to solve a puzzle are
$12, \ 15, \ 9, \ 14, \ 11, \ 17, \ 10, \ 16$
Calculate the mean and the population standard deviation, then find the $z$-score of the slowest time.
Give the standard deviation and the $z$-score correct to two decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Write the formula**
$z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$
2. **Substitute the value, the mean and the standard deviation**
From the statistics mode of the calculator,
$\mu = 13$
$\sigma = 2.7386...$
$\approx 2.74$
The slowest time is the largest, $x = 17$.
$z = \dfrac{17 - 13}{2.7386...}$
3. **Evaluate and round**
$= 1.4606...$
$\approx 1.46$

mastery.question_text:
A machine fills bottles with a mean of $502$ mL and a standard deviation of $1.6$ mL.
A bottle is rejected if its $z$-score is below $-2.5$ or above $2.5$.
Calculate the $z$-score, correct to two decimal places, of a bottle containing $497$ mL and state whether it is rejected.
mastery.solution_text:
$z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$
$= \dfrac{497 - 502}{1.6}$
$= \dfrac{-5}{1.6}$
$= -3.125$
$\approx -3.13$
The unrounded score is below $-2.5$, so the bottle is rejected.

Calculate the $z$-score of a runner who finishes in $23$ minutes.
